dedupe_keys.name: zorrotzaurre bilbao public private partnership for a flood proof district climate adapt

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study follows the redevelopment of Zorrotzaurre, a former industrial peninsula in the Bilbao estuary, into a flood-protected mixed district run by a public-private partnership, the Comisión Gestora de Zorrotzaurre, whose members pay costs in line with their land shares (51% public, 49% private). Flood measures are opening the Deusto canal to turn the peninsula into an island (opened October 2018), raising ground levels, a flood protection barrier and storm water tanks, alongside green public space; half of the new homes are social housing and two thirds of the area is for public uses. The canal cost about EUR 21 million, almost double the EUR 12.1 million estimate; the barrier costs EUR 1.68 million and the tanks were budgeted at EUR 5.7 million. A BC3 study estimates the measures remove damage from 10-year rainfall floods and cut damage by about 67% for 100-year and 30% for 500-year events, against metropolitan flood costs of EUR 5.5 million, 241 million and 444 million for those return periods. Coverage: one urban district, with works from 2016 and completion expected to take decades. Access: the case study page, published on 5 October 2016 and modified on 25 August 2026. Licence: Climate-ADAPT content under the EEA reuse policy; free. Caveats: benefits are modelled estimates; soil pollution and the 2008 crisis delayed the project. Simulation uses are validating flood damage reduction from district-scale measures in cost-benefit models. Related records: the Rouen Luciline and Maasbommel case studies.
